stem:
Vivek's class decides who can be called healthy. Health means physical, mental, and social well-being, not only the absence of disease.

They compare four classmates:
1  Walia has no disease, but she feels lonely, sleeps poorly, and avoids her classmates.
2  Xavier is free from illness, eats balanced food, stays cheerful, and shares a good bond with friends and family.
3  Uma has strong muscles and wins races, yet she often quarrels with everyone.
4  A classmate has had no fever this month, so nothing else is checked.

Whose situation shows complete health?

options.text: Walia has no disease, but she feels lonely, sleeps poorly, and avoids her classmates.
Xavier is free from illness, eats balanced food, stays cheerful, and shares a good bond with friends and family.
Uma has strong muscles and wins races, so she must be healthy even though she often quarrels with everyone.
A classmate has had no fever this month, so nothing else needs to be checked.

teacher.key_rationale: Complete health needs physical, mental, and social well-being. A and D treat disease absence alone as enough. C treats muscles and races as enough while social well-being fails.
